newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: South American port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: South American port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

ARGENTINA, April 8 - Santa Fe - No vessels berthed, none in roads, 1 due. Max. recommended draft 23 ft. 3 ins. at access channel. Diamante - One vessel berthed loading maize, 1 in roads, 1 due. Max. recommended draft 23 ft. 5 ins. at passage KM 520. San Lorenzo - Four vessels berthed, all loading, of which 1 by-products, 1 sbmp, 1 sbo, 1 sun oil. 7 Vessels in roads, 21 due at 6 terminals during this week and next. Max. recommended draft guided by Emilio Mitre channel, and forecast indicates a fall of about 0.15m during next week. Pasa berth draft - 25 ft. 2 ins. Fw.

Rosario - Five vessels berth of which 1 awaiting orders, 2 discharging fertiliser, 2 loading (1 sun oil, 1 sorghum). 1 Vessel in roads, 13 due during this week and next. Max. recommended draft guided by Emilio Mitre channel, and forecast indicates a fall of about 0.15m during next week. Villa Constitucion - One vessel berthed discharging iron ore, 1 in roads, 1 due. Elevator berths - Max. draft 22 ft. 0 ins. Fw. Max. recommended draft guided by Emilio Mitre channel. San Nicolas - Three vessels berthed of which 2 discharging coal, 1 loading soya. No vessels in roads, 5 vessels due within the next week. Max. recommended draft guided by Emilio Mitre channel, and forecast indicates a fall of about 0.15m during next week.

San Pedro - No vessels berthed, none in roads, 1 due. Max. recommended draft guided by Emilio Mitre channel, and forecast indicates a fall of about 0.15m during next week. Emilio Mitre channel - Max. recommended draft 32.00,33.00 ft.,fw. (high tide). Buenos Aires - 18 Vessels in port, 25 due within the next week. Max. recommended draft 31 ft. 6 ins. Fw. high tide Naabsa (guided by entrance channel). Dock sud - Max. draft 28,29 ft. Fw. High tide Naabsa (guided by Mitre channel). Necochea - Five vessels berthed of which 3 loading (2 wheat, 1 dap). 2 Discharging (1 sfmp, 1 sfo). 2 Vessels in roads, 10 due within the next week. Max. recommended draft at entrance channel 40 ft. 0 ins. Bw.

Bahia Blanca - Seven vessels berthed of which 1 awaiting orders. 6 Loading (1 barley, 2 maize, 1 crude oil, 1 sfo, 1 sfp). 1 Vessel in roads, 11 due within the next week. Drafts vary for individual berths.

BRAZIL, April 8 - Vitoria - Three vessels berthed of which 1 general cargo discharger/loader, 1 pig-iron loader, 1 granite loader. Tubarao - 3 Iron ore loaders, 1 fuel discharger. Praia Mole - 3 Steel products loaders, 1 coal discharger. Portocel - No vessels. Ubu - 1 Iron ore loader. 13 Vessels waiting in roads. Santos - 24 Vessels berthed of which 1 bulk diesel oil loader, 5 full container loaders/dischargers, 1 bulk cement, 3 general cargo/container loaders/dischargers, 1 general cargo discharger, 1 bulk soya loader, 2 container loaders, 1 bulk pellets loader/discharger, 3 fertiliser dischargers, 1 salt discharger, 1 general cargo/ro-ro loader/discharger, 3 chemical products loaders, 1 heavy lifts loader. 71 Vessels due over the next 7 days.

Private terminals - Cosipa - 1 Bulk coal discharger, 1 iron ore discharger. Ultrafertil - 1 Bulk sulphur discharger. Paranagua - 11 Vessels berthed of which 1 container discharger, 1 general cargo discharger, 2 fertiliser dischargers, 1 reefer loader, 4 pellets loaders, soya loader, 1 general cargo loader. 30 Vessels waiting in roads of which 27 to load (15 pellets, 12 soya). 3 To discharge (1 fertiliser, 1 containers, 1 general cargo). 28 Vessels due over the next 7 days.

Rio Grande - Seven vessels berthed of which 3 full containers, 1 barley discharger, 1 fertiliser discharger, 1 acid discharger, 1 chemical products, 2 vessels waiting in roads. 17 Vessels due over the next 10 days. Rio de Janeiro - 13 Vessels berthed of which 2 general cargo/container dischargers, 1 general cargo/steel products discharger, 1 wheat discharger, 2 general cargo dischargers, 1 paper discharger, 1 salt discharger, 2 oil dischargers, 2 steel products loaders, 1 general cargo loader. Tecon - 2 Vessels, 25 vessels due over the next 7 days. Sao Sebastiao - Tebar - 3 Vessels berthed. Commercial quay - 1 Vessel berthed, 3 waiting in roads, 12 due over the next 7 days.

CHILE, April 7 - Arica - One vessel at terminal, 5 berths vacant, 12 vessels due during the week. Iquique - Four vessels berthed and operating, 3 berths vacant, 6 vessels due during the week. Antofagasta - Two vessels berthed, 5 berths vacant, 3 vessels due during the week to load/discharge concentrates, bulk copper, containers and general cargo. Valparaiso - Seven vessels berthed and operating, 1 berth vacant, 1 berth (pier 3) out of order for enlargement until 16/4. 14 Vessels due during the week with 1 day's delay expected.

San Antonio - Five vessels operating, 5 berths vacant, 15 vessels due during the week. Port busy but no waiting time expected. Puerto Montt - Two vessels and 1 passenger vessel in port, 6 due during the week. Punta Arenas - One vessel berthed at terminal, 4 due during the week. Conception Bay ports - Talcahuano - One vessel berthed and operating, 5 due this week, none in roads. San Vicente - Three vessels berthed and operating, 1 berth vacant, 5 vessels due during the week, 1 day berthing delay expected.

Navy pier (Molo 500) - No vessels berthed, 2 due during the week. Steel pier - No vessels berthed, 4 due during the week, Coronel pier - 1 Vessel berthed. Oil terminal - No vessels berthed, 2 due during the week. Lirquen - Two vessels berthed, 3 berths vacant, 2 vessels due during the week. Penco - No vessels at terminal.

PERU, April 7 - No strikes at any port. Callao - Four vessels anchored, 5 general cargo/container vessels berthed, no berthing delays. Paita - No vessels anchored, none berthed, 2 days berthing delay expected for fish meal/general cargo vessels. Bayovar, Pisco - No vessels, no delays. Talara - One vessel anchored, 1 oil tanker berthed, no berthing delays. Chimbo - One fish meal vessel anchored, no vessels berthed, no berthing delays. Ilo - No vessels anchored, 1 fish meal vessel berthed, no berthing delays.

VENEZUELA, April 7 - Puerto Cabello - Nine vessels anchored of which of 5 grain cargo, 3 general cargo, 1 containers, 4 vessels berthed. Piers 1 and 2 closed. Guanta - Three general cargo vessels anchored, none berthed. April 8 - All ports working normally. Orinoco river - Draft 8/4, 30 ft. 0 ins. Puerto Ordaz - One vessel loading iron ore, 4 vessels due. Boca Grande - One vessel loading iron ore, 1 vessel due. Mile 178 - Two vessels waiting at anchorage to load. Palua - Two vessels due. Matanzas - Two vessels operating of which 1 loading steel products, 10 vessels due. Alcasa - One vessel discharging coke. Venalum - One vessel loading aluminium, 2 vessels due.

Interalumina - One vessel due. San felix - One vessel due. Punta Cuchillo - One vessel due. La Guaira - Five vessels loading/discharging general cargo, 2 due, 2 under repair. Puerto Cabello - 17 Vessels loading/discharging general cargo, 18 due. Amuay - Three vessels waiting at anchor to load, 7 loading refined products. Cardon - One vessel waiting at anchorage to load, 3 loading refined products. Guaranao - One vessel waiting at anchorage to load/discharge, 1 vessel discharging general cargo. Maracaibo - Five vessels loading/discharging general cargo.

Puerto Miranda - One vessel loading crude oil. El Tablazo - One vessel loading urea. Buoy B. 71 - One vessel loading coal. La Salina - One vessel loading crude oil. Bajo Grande - Refined products terminal - 2 Vessels loading refined products. La Ceiba - One vessel loading coal. Palmarejo Sur, Punta Palma, Punta Camacho, San Lorenzo, San Francisco - No vessels.
